Hello everyone,
I hope this email finds you well.

I have just started using this package to analyze Actigraphy data from the Parquet format. Since this data format is not supported by the package, I first converted it into CSV using R.
The dataset is structured with timestamp, acc_x, acc_y, and acc_z, which I believe are suitable for GGIR.

Given that my timestamps are in POSIX format, they include the "Z" (indicating the local time zone) after the time value. I mention this because, while reading the guide, I noticed that the example does not include the "Z" (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/readmyacccsv.html-Part3).

my file:
"TimeStamp,Accel_ax1,Accel_ax2,Accel_ax3
2023-03-31T17:09:18.000004Z,-0.65625,-0.125,0.703125"

My code:

GGIR(
  mode=c(1,2),
  datadir = "/Users/martinacarnevale/Desktop/TEST/input",
  outputdir = "/Users/martinacarnevale/Desktop/TEST/output",
  data_format = "actigraph_csv",
  read.myacc.csv(rmc.file=c("/Users/martinacarnevale/Desktop/try.csv"), rmc.nrow=Inf, rmc.dec=".",

Error: No milestone data found for part(s) 1. Run this/these first before running part 2.

Thank you in advance.

Best wishes,
Martina Carnevale

Re. 1. see parameter do.sibreport, <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#do-sibreport> which as of release 3.2-0 is TRUE by default.

Re. 2 the code checks whether parameter loglocation is non-empty. If yes, it concludes that sleep diary is present. By default loglocation is NULL. If you set it to a value, run GGIR, and then remove that line of code in GGIR, the value will still be in the config.csv file and retrieved by GGIR. So, to undo setting it to a value either explicitly set it to NULL or remove the config.csv file. This is also discussed here <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter2_Pipeline.html#parameter-extraction-order> in the documentation.

messages.body_plain:
Hello Martine,

As documented here <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/readmyacccsv.html>, always first try to run read.myacc.csv() on its own before providing the parameters values to the GGIR() function. By doing so you can test that your parameter values are correct by check that the output of the function is correct.

For example, I think timezone is reference with %Z and not with %OS, but you should find out quickly if you follow that approach. https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~s133/dates.html

Please note that even though you have the timezone there and should specify it, GGIR ignores this when actually processing the timestamps. Additionally, you always have to specify parameter desiredtz <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#desiredtz> to indicate the timezone your data was collected in, unless it is the timezone your computer is in, in which case you can keep the default value of "". If your recording was configured in a different timezone also consider parameter configtz <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#configtz>. These parameters ensure that day saving time is correctly accounted for.

> I also tryed using Actigraph datas from testifies https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/inst/testfiles/ActiGraph13.csv but it didn't work.

That does not work because it is not raw accelerometer data, but count data. The functionality  only works for raw data (multiple values per second).

Best,

Vincent

Hello Juan Pablo,

> when calculated using the sum of bouts_wei for MVPA.

Chile/Continental => Note that this does not account for day saving time. I would advise using a name that is specific to a city and country in your timezone such as America/Santiago. By doing so GGIR/R takes care of day saving time.

HASPT.algo ="HDZA", => does not exist, "HDCZA" is the correct name.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Marcello,

As Tom clarified, using of temperature data in the external function is not possible at the moment, unless you dive into the code and make your own edits like Tom did.

I designed the external function embedding option to aid deriving additional signal features (metrics), which are then treated by the rest of GGIR as any of the following:
scalar similar to ENMO, MAD, counts, etc.
event such as steps.
character which we used as indicator of sleep
Nonwear detection is not an option at the moment. So, even if your calculation would reflect an improved non-wear classification then GGIR will not be able to use it at the moment.

It may be easier to explore this as a direct addition to GGIR (via pull request) rather than as external function.

Let me know if you want to develop this.

Best wishes,

Vincent

Hi Maximilian,

Column name elements like D1 D2 etc are all ignored by GGIR. GGIR only checks whether the column name has a known character pattern such as "date", "onset", "inbed" etc. So, you can add whatever text you like to the column names as long as it does not overlap with the terms GGIR is looking for, unless you want it to overlap.

Yes, dates are critical for the advanced sleeplog format to work, because how else can GGIR know to which date a time belongs. See documentation for details.

Your issue is different to the one by Callum.

> Both part6CR and part6HCA are set to FALSE by which there is not analysis to be run in part 6.

This is a warning and NOT an error, I added it to the 3.2-0 release but accidentally it is also shown when part 6 is not run. This has now been fixed in the 3.2-1 release (GitHub only), but it does not affect your analysis. You can suppress the warning by setting part6CR = TRUE.

Best, Vincent

Hi Jayson,

> I am analyzing CWA files from the AX3 device. According to the AX3 datasheet, the APDS-9007 light sensor records logarithmic responses corresponding to human eye sensitivity. I would like to clarify whether the lux values in GGIR are derived directly from the device's raw output or if they result from an exponential transformation applied within GGIR.

By default LUX values are taken as they are without transformation.
However, with LUX_cal_constant <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#lux_cal_constant> and LUX_cal_exponent <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#lux_cal_exponent> you can tell GGIR to transform them. I had a project where the manufacturer instructed me to do the transformation for a specific set of old devices from 2012 that were not well calibrated. In that case, the transformation happens inside GGIR part 5.

 <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#lux_cal_exponent>
> Additionally, you mentioned that peak light exposure during a short period (e.g., 5 s) may be more reliable than the mean. Is there any evidence or research supporting this claim? Does GGIR support outputting light data in 1-second epochs from the meta folder?

It is likely that for some moments the sensor is facing away from the light source or even covered by a sleeve or blanket. Looking at 5-s summaries of the data would give us a mixture of true light exposure and the influence of those variations in posture and sensor coverage.

This is why GGIR by default takes the peak LUX value per 15 minutes, although 5 minutes should also work. By taking the peak light we are more likely to get a indicator of true light exposure for that period, while taking the mean would also reflect the degree to which the sensor was facing away from the light source or covered. To me this is common sense and I do not see why someone would go through the effort of doing a study about it. Although, it would be interesting to know what the optimal balance is between short and long window lengths. I do not know the literature well enough to know whether this has already been done. If you or someone else wants to help map out best practises around lux data processing please let me know. Help can be in the form of payment for my time or in the form of your own time investment.

Technically you can get lux output at a higher resolution. For example, setting parameter windows = c(5, 60, 3600) will make that LUX data is summarised per 1 minute (60 seconds). However, following the above, I do not think there is value in reducing this to 1 or 5 seconds. If you want to go that way then I think it is better that you work directly with the accelerometer data files and write your own custom code, because I expect that GGIR will be slow when you try this.

Best,

Vincent
